dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If ever you wish to rest without being interrupted by other people, there's a method I use occasionally that I can highly recommend.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Quite simply, fetch a brush and paper and start copying some poems. To the eye of the average observer, you will appear engrossed in official duties, and people will avoid disturbing you unless it's something particularly urgent.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Plus, the very practice of calligraphy induces a state of inner calm. Which is, of course, the main reason I recommend this technique.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It is often unwise to engage fearsome foes with brute force alone.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The first step should always be to analyze your enemy. Identify the source of his strength — this will point you towards his weakness, then you can direct your energies more efficiently in combat.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Call it cunning, if you will, but there is no shame in this. Extraordinary feats are accomplished through extraordinary measures.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I have heard that Mondstadt's deity makes few demands of his people. Whether they prosper or not, their fortunes are of their own making.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But is this a blessing or a poisoned chalice? In the quieter moments, I often find myself wondering what the merits of this approach to guardianship are...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, it is hardly my place to criticize. I simply desire to protect everyone I can.
